title: Ostra dark-mode restaurant menu: grade six mixed-lighting plate shots to one house white point, then author the hero + vectorize the wordmark
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for a premium restaurant website (a Portugal-based boutique digital agency wanting a 'high-end, clean, modern-minimalist' site with a 'Dark Mode aesthetic' that 'focuses heavily on high-quality food photography', Home / Interactive Food Menu / Booking sections, mobile-responsive). The real post had no brand name; the restaurant is laundered to a fictional fine-dining room, OSTRA, and the client stays an unnamed boutique studio whose own web designer builds the site (no real platform named). The web build itself is out of Adobe-connector scope (no layout composition, no web build), so the task is scoped to the brief's repeatedly-stressed pillar: the dark-mode food photography the whole site 'focuses heavily on.' ENRICHMENT (needed to make the chain concrete, failable, and measurable): the restaurant photographed SIX signature items across TWO service sessions under different mixed lighting, and the photographer clipped a neutral 18% grey reference chip + a small white chip to the edge of the board on every frame (standard tethered-shoot practice) so white balance can be reconciled after the fact. The six-shot count, the two-session lighting split, the in-frame reference chip, the stated per-shot casts, and the crop dimensions are reasonable enrichment; nothing contradicts the source (dark-mode look, food-photo emphasis, Home/Menu sections, mobile optimization are all from the brief).
one_line_ask: Turn OSTRA's six mixed-lighting raw plate shots into one cohesive dark-mode menu set that neutralizes to a single house white point and black-floor, author the signature dish into a desktop hero + mobile crop with clean headline negative space, and vectorize the flat wordmark for the dark site.
full_brief:
OSTRA is a new dark-room fine-dining restaurant. Our studio is building its premium website and the whole design leans on the food photography, shown dark-mode across the Home and Interactive Food Menu sections and on mobile. We are NOT reshooting and we do NOT need the site built here — our own web designer handles layout. We need a retoucher to turn our raw plate shots into a polished, cohesive dark-mode image pack.

What you're given: six raw signature-item captures, shot on two different nights under different mixed lighting so they do NOT match out of camera — three from warm tungsten dinner service (seared scallops, braised short rib, an amber cocktail), and three from a cooler prep-kitchen daylight setup (a chocolate fondant flat-lay, a burrata starter, oysters on ice). On the edge of the board in every frame the photographer left a neutral 18% grey chip and a small white chip as a white-balance reference — use them, then crop them out of the finals. The signature scallop frame also came in a few degrees off-level.

The bar (this is the whole job): the menu has to read as ONE room. Every dish must resolve to the SAME house look — a moody dark-mode grade where the neutral grey chip in each frame lands truly neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at one common white point, and the dark table surround floors at one common near-black level that is deep but NOT crushed to pure black and never clips a channel to zero. Because the six frames start from different casts and different exposures, matching the OUTPUT means each frame needs a DIFFERENT correction — the warm dinner shots pulled cooler and often lifted, the cool daylight shots warmed and usually pulled down. A set that was each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will not match at the grey chip, and we will reject it. Keep food tones appetizing — dark, not muddy; do not blow the specular highlight on the scallop sear or on glass and ice.

Deliverables: (1) the signature scallop dish as a full-bleed desktop HERO, perfectly level, graded to the house look, the plate lifted so it reads off the dark surround, reframed to a wide 16:9 with the dish sitting off to the right so the existing dark table gives our designer clean negative space on the left for an overlaid headline; (2) a full-bleed 9:16 MOBILE crop of that hero for the mobile Home; (3) five square 1:1 MENU-TILE images (short rib, cocktail, fondant, burrata, oysters) all graded to the same house look; (4) our flat wordmark logo cleaned to a transparent PNG and vectorized to a crisp SVG for retina use on the dark site. Along with the files, hand back a short sheet listing, per image, the white-balance (temperature / tint), exposure, and black-point values you dialed, so we can confirm the set was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.

inputs.name: raw_hero_scallops.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant food photograph, raw unretouched DSLR look, three pan-seared scallops with a golden crust on a dark charcoal slate plate, micro-herb garnish and a smear of pea puree, on a dark wooden restaurant table under warm mixed tungsten lighting (~3200K, strong warm/amber cast), slightly underexposed and flat contrast as if straight off the camera, horizon tilted about 4 degrees, a small neutral 18% grey card and a white chip resting on the table at the far LEFT edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, visible plate texture, real sear marks, condensation and tiny oil sheen on the scallops, candid documentary food shot, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: The HERO and the reference frame that establishes the house look. Deliberately tilted ~4deg (auto_straighten has work), warm tungsten cast + slightly underexposed (WB + exposure correction is real), and the grey/white chip sits at the FAR LEFT so it can be neutralized first and then cropped away when the plate is offset RIGHT for the 16:9 hero. Real food micro-detail, no CGI gloss.

inputs.name: raw_short_rib.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant food photograph, raw unretouched look, a glossy braised short rib with jus and a parsnip puree quenelle on a dark charcoal plate, dark wooden table, warm mixed tungsten dinner-service lighting (~3200K, warm amber cast), slightly underexposed, real braise sheen and meat fiber detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip on the table at the edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary food shot, no text, square 1:1
inputs.realism_notes: Session-A warm dish. Same warm cast as the hero but a slightly different exposure, so its correction toward the common target is close to the hero's but NOT identical — tests whether the agent reasons per-frame rather than copying the hero's numbers.

inputs.name: raw_cocktail_closeup.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant close-up photograph, raw unretouched look, an amber whiskey-sour cocktail in a coupe glass with a citrus twist and a thin foam layer, condensation on the glass, dark bar background slightly out of focus, warm tungsten bar lighting (~3200K, warm cast) that is also a touch BRIGHTER than the plated dishes, real glass refraction and bubble detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the lower edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, square 1:1
inputs.realism_notes: Session-A warm dish, but brighter than the food plates — so it needs the warm-to-neutral WB correction AND a downward exposure nudge, unlike the short rib which needs a lift. Two warm frames that still take different corrections.

inputs.name: raw_dessert_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal overhead flat-lay food photograph, raw unedited look, a molten chocolate fondant dusted with cocoa on a grey marble board, a single raspberry and gold-leaf garnish, cooler prep-kitchen daylight from a window (~5600K, distinctly cooler and brighter than the dinner-service shots), natural soft shadows, real crumb and melt detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip on the board at the edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, square 1:1
inputs.realism_notes: Session-B COOL dish. Cooler AND brighter than the hero, so the correct move is the OPPOSITE of the warm frames — warm the WB toward the target and pull exposure DOWN. This is the frame most likely to expose a naive 'apply the same numbers to all' or per-image auto-tone approach.

inputs.name: raw_burrata_starter.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal food photograph, raw unedited look, a creamy burrata starter torn open over heirloom tomatoes with basil oil and flaky salt on a dark ceramic plate, cooler prep-kitchen daylight (~5400K, cool neutral cast), slightly flat and a little bright, real creamy curd and tomato flesh texture, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, square 1:1
inputs.realism_notes: Session-B cool dish. Cool cast + slightly bright + flat contrast, needs warming toward the target and the shared dark-mode tone/black-floor — another opposite-direction correction from the warm frames, with white curd that will show any residual cast plainly.

inputs.name: raw_oysters_on_ice.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal food photograph, raw unedited look, six fresh oysters on crushed ice with a mignonette and lemon on a dark slate, cooler prep-kitchen daylight (~5800K, clearly cool/blue cast), bright specular glints on the wet shells and ice, real shell nacre and ice texture, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, square 1:1
inputs.realism_notes: Session-B cool dish, the coolest and brightest of all — strong blue cast plus blown-risk specular highlights on ice, so the correct grade warms the WB, pulls exposure down, and protects highlights while still hitting the shared black-floor. Its ice/shell whites are a sensitive check for residual cast at the common white point.

inputs.name: ostra_wordmark_logo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A minimalist flat restaurant wordmark logo, the single word OSTRA rendered in an elegant thin serif typeface, solid near-black charcoal lettering on a plain flat white background, a small leaf glyph as the dot over no letter but centered above the word, perfectly flat vector-style with crisp clean edges, no gradients no shadows no photographic texture, generous white margin around the mark, centered, high resolution
inputs.realism_notes: Flat solid-color wordmark on white so a white drop-out to transparency then a trim-to-bounds then a raster-to-vector trace produce a clean SVG. Crisp edges and a single dark ink color make the vectorize step honest; the generous white margin is what makes the trim-to-bounds prep step matter before tracing.

outputs.name: hero_dark_desktop.png
outputs.spec: Full-bleed desktop website hero, ~2880x1620 (16:9), straightened, graded to the OSTRA house look (grey chip neutralized to the common white point; dark table surround floored at the common near-black level, deep but not clipped to 0), the scallop plate lifted so it reads off the dark surround, reframed by an honest off-center crop of the native 3:2 so the plate sits RIGHT and the existing dark table forms clean headline negative space on the LEFT, grey/white reference chips cropped out of frame, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: hero_mobile_9x16.png
outputs.spec: Full-bleed mobile Home crop, 1080x1920 (9:16), subject-aware crop of the graded, popped full-res hero (existing pixels only, honest downscale, no upscale, no canvas extend), reference chips out of frame, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: menu_tile_short_rib.png
outputs.spec: Square 1:1 menu-tile (~1200x1200), graded to MATCH the house look at the common white point and black-floor, reference chips cropped out, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: menu_tile_cocktail.png
outputs.spec: Square 1:1 menu-tile (~1200x1200), graded to MATCH the house look at the common white point and black-floor, reference chips cropped out, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: menu_tile_fondant.png
outputs.spec: Square 1:1 menu-tile (~1200x1200), graded to MATCH the house look at the common white point and black-floor (warmed and pulled down from a cool/bright daylight raw), reference chips cropped out, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: menu_tile_burrata.png
outputs.spec: Square 1:1 menu-tile (~1200x1200), graded to MATCH the house look at the common white point and black-floor (warmed from a cool raw, white curd holding neutral), reference chips cropped out, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: menu_tile_oysters.png
outputs.spec: Square 1:1 menu-tile (~1200x1200), graded to MATCH the house look at the common white point and black-floor (strongest warm correction, highlights on ice protected), reference chips cropped out, sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: logo_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Transparent, cleanly vectorized OSTRA wordmark as crisp SVG for retina/responsive use on the dark site, produced by white drop-out then trim-to-bounds then raster-to-vector trace (plus the transparent-PNG intermediate).

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the six food frames, the white-balance temperature and tint, the exposure offset, and the black-point value that were applied, plus the single common house-target white point and black-floor level all six were matched to. This is the acceptance artifact — it makes 'the set is matched to one target' checkable, and the corrections must be non-identical across the warm vs cool frames.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: raw_hero_scallops.jpg, raw_short_rib.jpg, raw_cocktail_closeup.jpg, raw_dessert_flatlay.jpg, raw_burrata_starter.jpg, raw_oysters_on_ice.jpg, ostra_wordmark_logo.png
connector_workflow.note: Bring the six raw plate captures and the flat wordmark into the working project in one load so the grade and the logo cleanup can run against real asset references. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.
Level the ~4deg tilted horizon on raw_hero_scallops before any grading or reframing, so the later off-center crop is measured against a true horizon. Consumes the uploaded hero.

ESTABLISH the OSTRA house look on the signature frame and record it as the target the other five must hit. Using the neutral grey/white chip in the frame as reference, dial temperature COOLER and set tint to drive that chip to true neutral (kills the ~3200K warm cast), then build the dark-mode tonality with image_apply_adjustments primitives: set blacks so the dark table surround floors at the house near-black level (deep, not clipped — darkest tones held off zero), pull highlights to protect the scallop sear specular, lift shadows only enough to keep food out of mud, add modest clarity and vibrance. This is a reasoned authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. The agent must report the temp/tint/exposure/black values chosen here — they define the common target. Consumes step 2.
Select the scallop plate subject on the graded hero to drive a selective lift. Semantic subject selection (allowed); returns a mask URI. Consumes step 3.

Masked selective edit: apply a small exposure/clarity/vibrance lift to the plate subject ONLY, using step 4's mask, so the dish reads off the dark surround while the background black-floor set in step 3 is left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit — not a whole-image push that would also lift the surround and break the house black-floor. Consumes the step-3 image + step-4 mask.

Honest off-center reframe of the popped 3:2 hero to 16:9: crop with the scallop plate offset RIGHT so the existing dark table on the LEFT becomes clean headline negative space, and crop the far-left grey/white reference chips OUT of frame in the same move. Downscale/reframe of existing pixels only — the canvas is never grown beyond the source and no pixels are invented. Consumes step 5.
Resize the reframed 16:9 hero to the ~2880x1620 desktop full-bleed export dimensions. DELIVERABLE hero_dark_desktop.png. Consumes step 6.

Subject-aware 9:16 crop of the FULL-RES popped hero (step 5, ~3024x2016) resized to exactly 1080x1920, chips outside the crop. Cropping from the full-res popped hero rather than the already-cropped 2880x1620 desktop file keeps the 1080x1920 target gen-free (honest downscale, no upscale, no canvas extend). DELIVERABLE hero_mobile_9x16.png.

Grade raw_short_rib to the SAME target set in step 3, reasoning its own correction. It is warm (~3200K) like the hero but a touch differently exposed, so cool the WB to land its grey chip on the common white point and lift exposure slightly less/more than the hero as its own histogram requires, then match the house black-floor and dark-mode curve. The reported numbers should be close to the hero's but NOT copied. Consumes the uploaded short rib.
Crop the reference chip out and resize to the ~1200x1200 square tile. DELIVERABLE menu_tile_short_rib.png. Consumes step 9.

Grade raw_cocktail_closeup to the common target. Warm cast like the hero but BRIGHTER, so this frame needs the warm-to-neutral WB correction AND a downward exposure nudge (opposite exposure direction from the short rib), while still hitting the shared black-floor and protecting the glass/foam speculars. Report its distinct values. Consumes the uploaded cocktail.
Crop the reference chip out and resize to the ~1200x1200 square tile. DELIVERABLE menu_tile_cocktail.png. Consumes step 11.

Grade raw_dessert_flatlay to the common target — the OPPOSITE-direction correction. It is cool (~5600K) and brighter than the hero, so WARM the WB to neutralize its grey chip and pull exposure DOWN, then apply the shared dark-mode black-floor and curve so a bright daylight flat-lay reads as the same moody room. Copying the hero's cooling/lifting numbers here is exactly the trap that fails the match. Report its distinct values. Consumes the uploaded dessert.
Crop the reference chip out and resize to the ~1200x1200 square tile. DELIVERABLE menu_tile_fondant.png. Consumes step 13.

Grade raw_burrata_starter to the common target. Cool (~5400K), slightly bright and flat, so warm the WB toward neutral (watch the white curd, which shows any residual cast plainly), add contrast, and seat the black-floor at the house level. Its correction differs again from the fondant's because its cast and brightness differ. Report its distinct values. Consumes the uploaded burrata.
Crop the reference chip out and resize to the ~1200x1200 square tile. DELIVERABLE menu_tile_burrata.png. Consumes step 15.

Grade raw_oysters_on_ice to the common target — the strongest correction of the set. Coolest and brightest (~5800K, blue cast), so apply the largest warm WB shift and exposure pull-down, protect the blown-risk speculars on ice and wet shells (highlights held), and still land the grey chip on the common white point and the surround on the common black-floor. Report its distinct values. Consumes the uploaded oysters.
Crop the reference chip out and resize to the ~1200x1200 square tile. DELIVERABLE menu_tile_oysters.png. Consumes step 17.

Drop the flat white background of the wordmark to transparency so the mark sits cleanly on the dark site. White drop-out, no reconstruction. DELIVERABLE intermediate (transparent PNG). Consumes the uploaded logo.

Prep-before-trace: trim the transparent wordmark to its own tight bounds (removes the generous white margin now transparent) so the vectorize step traces only the lettering and leaf glyph. Tracing the untrimmed frame would waste trace resolution on empty canvas and can leave a stray border path. Consumes step 19.

Vectorize the trimmed transparent wordmark to crisp SVG for retina/responsive use on the dark site. Raster-to-vector trace of a prepared raster (straightened-by-nature flat mark, background knocked to transparency, cropped to bounds). DELIVERABLE logo_wordmark.svg. Consumes step 20.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining across four tributaries that converge on one cohesive dark-mode pack. HERO tributary (establishes the target): upload (1) -> auto_straighten (2) -> image_apply_adjustments (3, the REFERENCE house grade: grey chip neutralized to the common white point, surround floored at the common black level, dark-mode curve — this frame's reported temp/tint/exposure/black ARE the target) -> select_subject (4) -> image_apply_adjustments masked (5, subject-only lift using the step-4 mask) -> crop_and_resize (6, honest off-center 3:2->16:9 with the plate right, dark left negative space, chips cropped out) -> crop_and_resize (7, resize to ~2880x1620 = hero_dark_desktop). MOBILE (8) re-crops the full-res popped hero from step 5 to 1080x1920. Five MENU-TILE tributaries each fan out from assets_uploaded and each reason a DIFFERENT correction to the SAME target before a square resize: short rib (9->10, warm, near-hero but not copied), cocktail (11->12, warm + brighter so cool WB + pull down), fondant (13->14, cool+bright so warm WB + pull down, opposite of the warm frames), burrata (15->16, cool, warm WB, white curd holds neutral), oysters (17->18, coolest/brightest, largest warm shift + highlight protection). LOGO tributary: remove_background (19, white drop-out to transparent PNG) -> crop_to_bounds (20, prep-before-trace trim) -> vectorize (21, logo_wordmark.svg). Cross-asset consistency is NOT enforced by repeating one recipe — each of steps 9/11/13/15/17 is a distinct correction whose only invariant is the shared target white point and black-floor from step 3, and the agent reports all six so the match is auditable.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon food_bev_photo retouch scoped from the real brief's stressed pillar. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth: (a) cross-asset grade-MATCH of six differently-lit frames to a single measurable house target — a common white point read off each frame's in-frame grey chip and a common near-black floor — which forces non-identical per-frame corrections (three warm dinner frames cooled/lifted, three cool daylight frames warmed/pulled-down), authored from image_apply_adjustments primitives rather than a preset or auto-tone; (b) a masked selective lift on the hero (select_subject -> masked image_apply_adjustments) that must pop the plate WITHOUT lifting the surround that the black-floor depends on; (c) an honest two-stage gen-free reframe of the 3:2 hero to a 16:9 with left headline negative space that also crops the reference chips out; and (d) prep-before-trace logo discipline (white drop-out -> trim-to-bounds -> vectorize). The agent must report its final per-image parameters, making 'matched' checkable. Every step is headless-confirmed [C], server=adobe: no [W] Express widget, no [A] async media, no [T] template. No banned capability: no generative expand/outpaint, no gen-fill, no upscale/super-resolution, no text-to-image, no object-removal-with-reconstruction, no image_fill_area, no whole-image color_overlay sold as a masked edit, no render_* layout authoring; the web build is correctly out of scope.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE: the acceptance artifact is a single matched dark-mode set — every frame's neutral grey chip must resolve to ONE common house white point and the dark surround to ONE common near-black floor (deep but not clipped to zero), and the agent must return a parameter sheet listing per-image temperature/tint/exposure/black. This is tripable: a set that is each internally 'auto-fixed' will diverge at the grey chips and be rejected, and identical reported numbers across warm and cool frames are a visible fail. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across six frames shot under two opposite casts, which demands the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT requires DIFFERENT per-frame corrections (warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed) reasoned from each frame's own chip and exposure — not one set of sliders; (2) a masked subject-only lift on the hero that must brighten the plate while preserving the surround black-floor the whole house look depends on; plus prep-before-trace logo discipline. TRAP: the naive path — run auto-tone (or one dark preset) on each of the six and call it a matched set — looks right because every frame reads fine alone, but auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram, so the cool daylight dishes stay cooler/brighter than the warm dinner frames, the grey chips do not agree, and the set fails the one-white-point gate; a second trap is copying the hero's exact temp/exposure onto the opposite-cast daylight frames, and a third is cropping the reference chips out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the WB reference). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE: grey chip neutral (R≈G≈B) at the common white point on all six, surround black-floor at the shared near-black level with no channel clipped to 0, hero straightened and reframed to 16:9 ~2880x1620 with left negative space and chips removed, mobile at exactly 1080x1920, tiles ~1200x1200, logo delivered as transparent PNG + trimmed SVG, and the returned per-image parameter sheet must show non-identical corrections converging on the stated target.
